main_text.p: 1. Pet. 3. v.18. Ille, qui purgatione peccatorum nostrorum per feipsum facta, consedit ad dextram Majestatis in excelsis, Heb. 1. v. 3. ille qui Mediator inter Deum & Homines est: 1. Tim. 2. v. 5. ille qui est caput Ecclesiæ, Ephes. 1. v. 22. ille denique qui est Sacerdos & Rex unicus. Hebræor. 2. v. 7. 24. 25. Apocal. 19. vers. 16.

Hic est salutis no-stra acqui-sitor seu servator noster.IV. De hoc, inquam, Jesu Christo dicitur in quæstione, quod salutem æ-ternam a nobis acquisierit, adeoq; sit Servator noster, seu salutis æternæ Auctor, Princeps Vitæ talis, qui nos ab æterna damnatione & potestate tenebrarum, a servitute & reatu peccati liberavit: & contra beatam vitam ac immortalitatem nobis comparavit. Hebræor. 5. v. 9. Hic consecratus factus est AUCTOR SALUTIS ÆTERNÆ omnibus qui auscultant ipsi. Actor. 3. v. 15.

Principem vitæ trucidastis, quem Deus excitavit a mortuis, cujus rei nos testes sumus. Hebræor. 2. v. 14. 15. Quoniam igitur pueri participes sunt carnis & sanguinis, ipse quoq; consimiliter particeps factus est eorundem, ut per mortem aboleret eum, qui mortis imperium ha-

page.notes: Page number "41" printed at the top right as "4ᵻ"; read as 41. Actor. 3. v. 15 reference: the numeral is read as 3 on the scan (the Acts reference "auctorem vitae" fits 3:15), please check. Hebræor. 5. v. 9: the numeral is printed like a long s, read as 5. Spelling "feipsum", "est", "salutis" etc. kept as printed. Margin note marked "4." in the margin, with no matching mark in the text. Catchword "bet," read at the lower right, end of the paragraph is hyphenated "ha-".
